'''Joseph David Brain''' (January 20, 1940 – January 29, 2024) was an American [[Physiology|physiologist]] and [[environmental health]] researcher, who served as the Cecil K. and Philip Drinker Professor of Environmental Physiology at [[Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health]],<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.hsph.harvard.edu/joseph-brain/ |title=Joseph Brain |publisher=harvard.edu |accessdate=April 30, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://environment.harvard.edu/about/faculty/joseph-brain |title=Joseph Brain |work=Harvard University Center for the Environment |date=7 October 2010 |publisher=harvard.edu |accessdate=April 30, 2017 |author1=Anonymous }}</ref> where he taught and researched for over fifty years.

==Early life==
Born in [[Paterson, New Jersey]] and raised in [[Wayne, New Jersey]], Brain attended [[Eastern Christian High School]] in [[North Haledon, New Jersey]],<ref name=Facebook>[https://www.facebook.com/joseph.brain.7 Joe Brain], [[Facebook]]. Accessed December 27, 2023.</ref> after which he went in 1957 to [[Taylor University]] in [[Upland, Indiana]], where he majored in [[physics]].  After his graduation from (then) Taylor College, Brain was offered the [[Danforth Foundation]] Graduate Fellowship (1961–1966) at Harvard.<ref name="CV for Joseph David Brain">{{Cite web |url=http://www.ibrarian.net/navon/paper/CURRICULUM_VITAE_I__BIOGRAPHICAL_INFORMATION.pdf?paperid=643334 |title=CV for Joseph David Brain |access-date=2017-05-29 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171231212013/http://www.ibrarian.net/navon/paper/CURRICULUM_VITAE_I__BIOGRAPHICAL_INFORMATION.pdf?paperid=643334 |archive-date=2017-12-31 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==Education==
* High School Diploma, 1957, [[Eastern Christian High School]], [[North Haledon, New Jersey]]<ref name=Facebook/><ref name=News1966>[https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-news-doctorate-awarded-to-joseph-d/137471971/ "Brain Awarded Physiology Doctorate"], ''[[Herald News|Paterson News]]'',  July 11, 1966. Accessed December 27, 2023, via [[Newspapers.com]]. "Joseph D. Brain, son of Mr. and Mrs. Dow Brain of 9 Bertrand Drive, was awarded a doctor of science degree in physiology from Harvard University, Cambridge, Mass. Dr. Brain, a graduate of Eastern Christian High School. North Haledon, and Taylor University, Upland, Ind., will be a research associate and teacher in the physiology department at Harvard."</ref>
* B.A. (Physics, Summa cum laude), 1961, [[Taylor University]], [[Upland, Indiana]]<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.taylor.edu/euler/programs/service.shtml |title=Kingdom Service: Profile of Joseph Brain, Taylor University |access-date=2017-05-09 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131111070857/http://www.taylor.edu/euler/programs/service.shtml |archive-date=2013-11-11 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>[https://www.linkedin.com/in/joe-brain-29834a6/ LinkedIn profile for Joe Brain]</ref><ref name=News1966/>
* S.M., 1962, [[Harvard John A. Paulson School of Engineering and Applied Sciences|Harvard Paulson School of Engineering and Applied Sciences]] - on [[Danforth Foundation]] Graduate Fellowship (1961–1966)
* S.M., 1963, [[Harvard John A. Paulson School of Engineering and Applied Sciences|Harvard Paulson School of Engineering and Applied Sciences]] - on [[Danforth Foundation]] Graduate Fellowship (1961–1966)
* S.D., 1966, [[Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health]] - on [[Danforth Foundation]] Graduate Fellowship (1961–1966)<ref name=News1966/>

==Career==
Brain served as the Cecil K. and [[Philip Drinker]] Professor of Environmental Physiology<ref>[https://alumni.neurosurgery.mgh.harvard.edu/docs/Harvard_Professorsips_Book_1721-1992.pdf Harvard Named Chairs, page 354.  The Drinker Chair was funded by James Henry Rand (1886-1968)]</ref> at [[Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health]], and participated in the leadership of [[Bernard Lown#The Lown Institute and the Right Care Alliance|The Lown Institute]].<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.lownfoundation.org/lown_scholars_program.html | title=Lown Scholars Program }}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.hsph.harvard.edu/lownscholars/steering-committee/ | title=Steering Committee | date=21 December 2018 }}</ref>  After graduation from Taylor, Brain was offered the Danforth Foundation Graduate Fellowship (1961–1966) at Harvard.<ref name="CV for Joseph David Brain"/>

Brain took part in a five-year collaboration signed between the [[University of Malaya]] (UM) and [[Harvard University]] in the search for more effective treatment of lung diseases through [[nanomedicine]]. In 1998, he was named the Director of the Kresge Center for Environmental Health at Harvard.

Brain was director of Respiratory Biology Program (1981–1993) and Physiology Program (1993–1997). He was also chair of the Department of Environmental Health at Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health (1990–2005).

==Personal life and death==
Brain was married and lived in [[Essex, Massachusetts]]. He served on the Taylor University Board of Trustees from 1988 to 2009.

Joseph Brain died on January 29, 2024, at the age of 84.<ref name="death-announcement">{{Cite web|url=https://countway.harvard.edu/news/memory-joe-brain |last1=Novak Gustainis |first1=Emily R. |last2=Podolsky |first2=Scott H. |last3=Martin |first3=Elaine |title=In memory of Joe Brain |publisher=Harvard Countway Library |date=February 5, 2024 |access-date=February 6, 2024}}</ref>

==Honors==
* [[U.S. Atomic Energy Commission]] Fellowship in [[Health physics|Health Physics]] 1961–1962
* Danforth Foundation Graduate Fellowship 1961–1966
* USPHS Radiological Health Fellowship 1962–1966
* NIH Research Career Development Award 1969–1974
* Aaron Brown Lecturer ([[University of Pittsburgh]]) 1981
* [[American Men and Women of Science]] 1982
* Alumnus of the Year, [[Taylor University]] 1984
* Fellow, [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]] 1987
* [[NIH MERIT Award]] 1987–1995
* Henry D. Chadwick Medal, Massachusetts Thoracic Society 1993
* Honorary Professor of [[Huazhong University of Science and Technology]] (HUST), 1999, [[Wuhan, China]]
* Recognition of Merit, Librarians, Archivists, and Museum Professionals in the History of the Health Sciences's (LAMPHHS), 2022<ref>[https://countway.harvard.edu/news/memory-joe-brain  Gustainis ERN, Podolsky SH, Martin E. In memory of Joe Brain. Harvard Center for the History of Medicine. Countway Medical Library. President and Fellows of Harvard College, February 5, 2024.]</ref>
